## The Lens

::: {.checklist-grid}
::: {.check-section}
### 1. Collaboration Design

State what moves: patient-level data, model updates, metrics, aggregate counts, or only conclusions. Explain why that movement is scientifically and legally justified.
:::
::: {.check-section}
### 2. Institution As A Variable

Plan analyses by site from the start. Describe scanner, assay, referral, label, annotation, and workflow differences as measurable context rather than noise.
:::
::: {.check-section}
### 3. Missingness And Modality

Make a modality-by-site matrix before modelling. Distinguish random absence from workflow, access, disease severity, and historical documentation patterns.
:::
::: {.check-section}
### 4. Site-Level Evaluation

Predefine global, per-site, worst-site, subgroup, calibration, uncertainty, abstention, unseen-site, and temporal-drift reporting.
:::
::: {.check-section}
### 5. Privacy As Information Flow

Write a threat model in plain language: who can see what, what can be inferred, what is logged, what is released, and who responds to incidents.
:::
::: {.check-section}
### 6. Governance And Maintenance

Name owners for clinical validity, data quality, security, ethics, contracts, authorship, model updates, withdrawal, and postdeployment monitoring.
:::
:::

## Protocol Sentence Starters

- "The primary collaboration design is ... because ..."
- "Patient-level data will not move; the following information will move ..."
- "Institution will be analysed as a source of clinical and measurement variation by ..."
- "The study will be considered unsuccessful if any site or subgroup falls below ..."
- "The privacy claim is limited to ... and does not cover ..."
- "The model will be maintained, recalibrated, or retired when ..."
